items.question: How long does it take to build an agent?
items.answer: A working first version usually takes less than a month. Getting it into production with your data, permissions and approvals takes around three months. From there it grows with your needs.

items.question: What return can we expect, and how do you measure it?
items.answer: Before we build anything, we measure how long the task takes today and how often it runs. After launch we measure again. The return is the time saved multiplied by the cost of that time, minus what the agent costs to run. If the numbers do not justify an agent, we tell you.

items.question: Do you build custom agents or use ready-made ones?
items.answer: Both. Where a ready-made tool does the job, we set it up and connect it. Where your process is specific, we build a custom agent around it. The choice depends on what gets you the result fastest and cheapest.

items.question: Where is our data processed, and is it used for training?
items.answer: We use enterprise AI plans whose terms exclude training on your data. Where your rules require it, we host models and data on infrastructure you control. Processing follows the GDPR, and we document where every piece of data goes.

items.question: What happens after launch?
items.answer: We monitor the agent, fix what breaks and improve it as your process changes. You can keep us on a support plan or take it over fully.

items.question: Can our team maintain the agents ourselves?
items.answer: Yes. We work alongside your team, document everything and train the people who will own the agent, so you are never locked in.

items.question: Where should we start?

items.question: Can the AI make things up?

items.question: How long does it take?

items.question: What drives the cost?

items.question: Where should we start?

items.question: How do we know how reliable it will be?

items.question: Can AI read handwriting?
items.answer: Often, yes. OCR alone struggles with handwriting, while recent AI models do much better, especially on a clear photo. Results vary from one document to the next, which is why we test on yours and a person reviews every uncertain reading.

items.question: What drives the cost and the timeline?

A first version can come quickly: for a start-up that makes a CRM, we built a working document agent from scratch in one week.

items.question: Does it work with the tools we already use?

items.question: Where do our documents go?

mcp.summary: Connect your CRM, ERP and documents to AI with controlled access, so it answers from your real data instead of guessing.

faq.title: Questions about the Model Context Protocol

items.question: Where should we start?
items.answer: With a question your team asks often, whose answer sits in one or two tools. On a first 30-minute call, we look with you at which sources to connect first and which can wait.

items.question: Will it work with the tools we already use?
items.answer: With most of them, as long as they have an API or a database we can reach. Some vendors already offer an MCP server; if not, we build one. Because MCP is an open standard, your connections keep working if you switch AI models.

items.question: Can AI change our data?
items.answer: Only if you decide it can. By default we give read-only access. Write access is opened tool by tool, on a clearly defined scope, with human approval for sensitive actions.

items.question: Where does our data go?
items.answer: We favour hosting in Europe and enterprise AI plans that do not train on your data. AI only sees what the MCP server passes to it, and every access is logged.

items.question: Will AI make fewer mistakes?
items.answer: Yes, fewer. It answers from your data instead of guessing. The risk does not go away, though: we test on real cases, ask AI to show its sources, and keep a human check wherever a mistake would be costly.

items.question: What drives the cost and the timeline?
items.answer: Mostly the number of tools to connect and how easy they are to reach. A tool with a documented API connects quickly; older software without one takes more work. We follow the protocol closely, so we can tell you early what will be simple and what will not.

items.question: Where should we start?

items.question: Do we have enough data?
items.answer: Often more than you think: sales, invoices, CRM, spreadsheets. You usually need a history that covers several cycles of your business, for example at least two full seasons if your activity is seasonal. If you do not have that yet, we tell you before anything starts.

items.question: How reliable will the forecasts be?
items.answer: A forecast is never a certainty. We deliver it with a range and the factors that explain it, then measure the gap with reality on a regular basis. If the model does not beat your current method, we do not roll it out.

items.question: Do we need new software?
items.answer: No. Forecasts show up in your ERP, your CRM, your spreadsheets or a simple dashboard, and alerts come by email or in your team chat.

items.question: Where does our data go?
items.answer: We favour hosting in Europe and use only the data the model actually needs. When customer data is involved, we check the GDPR side with you before we start.

items.question: What drives the cost and the timeline?
items.answer: Mostly the state of your data: spread across several files, incomplete, or already clean. The number of sources to connect and of tools where forecasts should appear matters too. After the first call, we give you a clear estimate.

computer-vision.summary: Your photos and video become data: defects spotted, plates and meters read, stock counted. Your team stays in charge of the decisions.
computer-vision.intro: Computer vision teaches software to recognise what it sees in a photo or a video. We use it to pull one precise fact out of your images, such as a defect, a reading or a count, which then triggers an action in your tools.

included.title: What we do for you
included.intro: Concrete examples of tasks where images save time, while your team keeps the decisions.

items.title: Quality inspection
items.text: A camera on the line spots scratches, badly fitted parts or crooked labels. A doubtful part is set aside and photographed for your quality manager.

items.title: Meter readings
items.text: Your technicians take a photo of the water, gas or electricity meter. The reading goes straight into your tracking tool, with no copying by hand.

items.title: Plates and labels
items.text: Number plates are read at the entrance to a car park or a loading bay. On parcels, the product code and batch number are picked up automatically.

items.title: Photo checks
items.text: Move-in inspections, site photos, claim photos, ID documents: AI checks that each image is sharp, complete and consistent with the file before a person signs it off.

items.title: Site safety
items.text: Missing helmet or hi-vis vest, restricted area entered, blocked aisle: an alert goes to the site manager. We set it up with you so it respects GDPR and your staff.

items.title: Stock counts
items.text: A photo of a shelf, a pallet or a storage bay is enough to count items and spot gaps. You can run stock checks more often and spend fewer hours on them.

explainer.title: How we work
explainer.intro: Four steps, from the first image analysed to everyday use on the ground.

points.title: AI assessment
points.text: We start from a concrete problem, such as a defect that slips through or a stock count that takes too long, and check with you that images can answer it.

points.title: Process redesign
points.text: We decide who gets the alert, what the system does on its own and what a person confirms. We also work with real conditions: lighting, camera angles, the cameras you already have.

points.title: From pilot to rollout
points.text: A pilot runs on your own photos and video, and we measure what is recognised well and what is not. If the results hold up, we roll it out across your sites and tools.

points.title: Training and governance
points.text: We train the people who handle alerts, track accuracy over time and retrain the model when your products or premises change. GDPR and the EU AI Act are covered, especially whenever people appear on camera.

items.question: Where should we start?
items.answer: With a task where someone looks at images or objects today to make a call: inspecting, counting, reading. On a first 30-minute call, we tell you honestly whether computer vision is the right answer, or whether a sensor or a simple rule would do.

items.question: Do we need new cameras?
items.answer: Not necessarily. A smartphone or the cameras you already have are often enough to start. We check image quality during the pilot and only recommend hardware if the results call for it.

items.question: Do you train a custom model?
items.answer: Not always. To read text or recognise common objects, existing models often do the job. For a defect specific to your products, we train a model on your own images, including examples of faulty parts.

items.question: What happens when the system gets it wrong?
items.answer: It will happen, as it does to any person doing inspections. We measure the error rate before launch, set a confidence threshold below which a person checks, and keep tracking results over time.

items.question: What drives the cost and the timeline?
items.answer: Mostly the image work: how many images are needed, and whether they have to be labelled by hand, which means marking what each one shows. Then the number of sites, the hardware and the tools to connect. A narrow use case with photos you already have moves much faster than equipping a production line.

items.question: What about images that show people?
items.answer: We favour hosting in Europe, or processing on site when possible. As soon as a person or a number plate is in the picture, we keep only what is needed, can blur faces and plates, and agree the rules of use with you under GDPR and the EU AI Act.

ai-sprint.intro: In one day, on site or remote, we go through your operations with the people who run them. You leave with costed AI use cases, ranked by priority, and a clear plan for what comes next.

items.title: Workshops with your team

items.title: Finding the heavy tasks
items.text: Data typed in twice, piles of documents, the same errors again and again, manual reminders: we note what costs your team the most time.

items.title: Costed use cases
items.text: For each idea, we estimate the expected gain, how feasible it is, the risks to quality and data, and a rough cost.

points.title: AI assessment
points.text: This is the day itself: we look at your operations with your team and find the tasks where AI can bring a measurable gain.

points.title: Process redesign

points.title: From pilot to rollout

items.question: How much does an AI Sprint cost?
items.answer: It depends on the scope: how many teams and topics, on site or remote, travel. We agree the price with you before the day.

items.question: On site or remote?
items.answer: Both work. On site, we see your tools and the way people work up close. Remote, the day runs on a video call, with screen sharing so we can look at your tools together.

items.question: Who should take part?
items.answer: Someone from management to make the calls, people who live the processes day to day, and your IT lead or IT provider when data and tools are involved.

items.question: Do we need to know what we want from AI already?
items.answer: No. A hunch is enough, and so is no idea at all. The day starts from your real tasks, not from the technology.

items.question: What do we get at the end?
items.answer: A list of costed, ranked AI use cases, each with its expected gain, effort and risks, and a written roadmap.

items.question: What happens after the day?
items.answer: That is up to you. You can run the roadmap in-house or with another provider. If you want, we move on to a first prototype, with a Qartmina project lead and specialists picked for the job.

items.question: What drives the cost?
items.answer: Mainly the number of screens and business rules, how many tools need connecting and the level of security required. We start with a lean first version, then add what proves useful.

items.question: How long does it take?
items.answer: It depends on scope. A first usable version can come quickly: we built the MVP (a first working version cut down to essentials) of a document-processing agent from scratch in one week. You get a precise timeline at the end of scoping.

items.question: Will it work with the tools we already use?

items.question: Where is our data hosted?

items.question: How do you keep the tool reliable?
items.answer: Automated tests check the tool every time the code changes, and every delivery goes through a quality check. Once it is live, we monitor it and fix issues as part of maintenance.

items.answer: No. We handle the design, build, hosting, security and maintenance. Your team brings the method and reviews the output.

items.answer: You share your documents, frameworks and examples. We turn them into the agent's knowledge and rules, then test it with you case by case until the answers meet your standard. After launch you can keep updating its knowledge yourself.
